def verify_solution(solution):
    n = len(solution)
    # Check all pairs
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            # Same column
            if solution[i] == solution[j]:
                return False, f"Queens at rows {i} and {j} share column {solution[i]}"
            # Same diagonal
            if abs(i - j) == abs(solution[i] - solution[j]):
                return False, f"Queens at rows {i} and {j} are on same diagonal"
    return True, "Valid solution"

# Let's also find all solutions using backtracking
def solve_n_queens(n):
    solutions = []
    def backtrack(row, cols, diag1, diag2, current):
        if row == n:
            solutions.append(current[:])
            return
        for col in range(n):
            d1 = row - col  # main diagonal
            d2 = row + col  # anti-diagonal
            if col not in cols and d1 not in diag1 and d2 not in diag2:
                cols.add(col)
                diag1.add(d1)
                diag2.add(d2)
                current.append(col)
                backtrack(row + 1, cols, diag1, diag2, current)
                current.pop()
                cols.remove(col)
                diag1.remove(d1)
                diag2.remove(d2)
    
    backtrack(0, set(), set(), set(), [])
    return solutions

all_solutions = solve_n_queens(4)
print(f"\nAll solutions for 4-Queens: {all_solutions}")
